claims.claim: Sanford Lake, Wisconsin, is a 36-ha lake
claims.location: p. 10 (PDF p. 20), Study site; p. 11 (PDF p. 21), Figure 1
claims.quote: has an area of 35.6 ha, a length of l.13 km
claims.conditions: Sanford Lake, Vilas County, near Boulder Junction; drainage lake, maximum depth 15.5 m, shoreline 3.9 km

claims.note: Short gives no colour value: he says only that the lake is 'stained with tannic acid' (p. 13, PDF p. 23). The research note's 'colour 30 Pt-Co, pH 5.9, alkalinity 6 mg/L' does not come from Short (whose alkalinity is 9.0 ppm MOA); it may come from Saunders 2006 or a WDNR record, not checked here. Cite that source for the 30 Pt-Co, or write 'tannin-stained'.

claims.claim: Sanford Lake is tannin-stained, soft-water with 9 ppm alkalinity, and rich in wood
claims.quote: slightly alkaline (9.0 ppm, MOA), and stained with tannic acid
claims.conditions: methyl orange alkalinity; the lake is described as 'unproductive'; Big Crooked Lake, by contrast, is 15.0 ppm and 'very clear'
claims.note: Wood: 'Trees that fall into the lake provide abundant large woody structure throughout the littoral zone' (same page).

claims.claim: Sanford Lake's bed from 0 to 3 m was 70.0 % silt and about 6 % gravel or coarser
claims.location: p. 19 (PDF p. 29), Results, Available habitat; transects p. 15 (PDF p. 25); Appendix A (PDF p. 88)
claims.quote: 70.0% of the littoral zone in Sanford Lake was covered by silt
claims.conditions: 100 random transects from the water's edge to 3.0 m depth, a 1-m² quadrat every 2 m, particle sizes estimated visually (silt < 0.2 mm, sand 0.2–6.3, gravel 6.4–76, cobble 76.1–149.9, rubble 150–303.9 mm, boulders larger); the rest: sand 12.7, coarse organic debris 4.4, gravel 1.9, cobble 1.4, rubble 1.2, small boulders 1.1, large boulders 0.3 %
claims.note: Gravel + cobble + rubble + boulders = 1.9 + 1.4 + 1.2 + 1.1 + 0.3 = 5.9 % ≈ 6 %. Short also notes coarser substrates sit at the margins and silt increases with depth.

claims.claim: smallmouth nests reach 13 per km of shore (1.43/ha) at Sanford Lake
claims.location: p. 61 (PDF p. 71), Chapter II Table 1 (n = 51 nests, 1998); shoreline and area p. 10 (PDF p. 20)
claims.conditions: 1998; the whole littoral zone was searched by snorkel or SCUBA every other day through the spawning season (p. 55, PDF p. 65), so the 51 nests are the lake's census
claims.note: 51 nests / 3.9 km of shoreline = 13.1 per km; 51 / 35.6 ha = 1.43 per ha. Neither figure is printed by Short: the paper should mark both 'project arithmetic'.

claims.claim: on-nest survival at Sanford Lake averaged 22.7 %
claims.location: p. 61 (PDF p. 71), Chapter II Table 1; p. 66 (PDF p. 76), Discussion
claims.conditions: 1998, 51 nests; 'Mean survival represents the number of pre-swimup black fry on each nest as a percentage of eggs fertilized just after spawning' (mean ± 1 SE); eggs and black fry estimated visually with a grid, validated against counts (within ± 7 %)
claims.note: This is the mean of per-nest percentages; the pooled lake total is 31,470 / 101,935 = 30.9 % (the text's '69%' mortality). Big Crooked Lake: 72.7 %. Three high-quality nests produced 33 % of Sanford's swim-up fry.

claims.paper: Table 3.6-5 (smallmouth bass, Sanford and Big Crooked row)
claims.claim: eggs to autumn age 0: 0.64 % (Sanford, tannin-stained) and 4.8 % (Big Crooked, clear)
claims.location: p. 61 (PDF p. 71), Chapter II Table 1; p. 60 (PDF p. 70), Results
claims.conditions: 1998; age 0+ abundance by Chapman–Petersen mark–recapture in the fall (seine marking at nine stations, night electrofishing recapture within 3 weeks); Big Crooked row: 202,100 eggs, 146,475 black fry, 9,798 age 0+ (95.2 % mortality)
claims.note: 650 / 101,935 = 0.64 %; 9,798 / 202,100 = 4.85 %. Short's own conclusion: despite this, 'survival from eggs through age 0+ was not significantly different' between the lakes (ANCOVA, Table 2, p. 63) — worth a word in the table note.

claims.location: p. 61 (PDF p. 71), Chapter II Table 1; area p. 10 (PDF p. 20)
claims.conditions: 1998 fall mark–recapture estimate of 650 age 0+ for the whole 35.6-ha lake

notes: Other values: nests at 0.5–3.0 m with > 40 % gravel, not heavily embedded; no nests below 3.0 m in either lake; nest substrate in Sanford sand 20.6–28.1 %, gravel 57.7–63.2 %, cobble 5.7–23.8 % (1997, 1998); Big Crooked survival fell when nests were < 10 m apart; Sanford's best survival model (R² 0.47) = % cobble, water depth, distance to wood cover, male length. The research note's colour/pH/alkalinity line for Sanford (30 Pt-Co, pH 5.9, 6 mg/L) conflicts with Short's 9.0 ppm MOA and should be traced to its real source.
